findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. For user_count = 100 and limit = 50 this gives 3 pages, but only 2 pages of members exist. The pager shows a phantom page 3, and clicking next moves to offset 100, which returns an empty list. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit), with a minimum of 1 when user_count > 0.

findings.title: next() clamps offset to user_count instead of the start of the last page
findings.body: offset is set to Math.min(offset + limit, user_count). With user_count = 120 and limit = 50, the sequence goes 0, 50, 100, then 120. Offset 120 is past the end and returns no rows. The offset should be capped at the start of the last page, for example (totalPages - 1) * limit, not at user_count.

findings.title: alias_level chosen for a new group is never persisted
findings.body: For a new group, save() calls group.create(), which posts asJSON() including alias_level. The controller's create action ignores alias_level, and the JS create() does not follow up with a save. The user's alias level selection is silently dropped on creation and the group keeps the default.

findings.title: create action ignores alias_level sent by the client
findings.body: The client's asJSON() sends alias_level, but create only reads name and visible. Any alias_level value is discarded, so the admin UI cannot set alias level at creation time, and the behaviour differs from update.

findings.title: automatic flag is read from the member, not the group, so remove links show on automatic groups
findings.body: group_member.hbs is rendered as an itemView of each member, so its context is the User, not the group. {{#unless automatic}} therefore always evaluates true, and the remove link appears even for automatic groups. The server rejects those removals with a 422, but the UI still offers an action that cannot succeed. The automatic flag must be passed in from the group.

findings.title: limit and offset are unvalidated and can produce SQL errors or unbounded queries
findings.body: params[:limit] and params[:offset] are converted with to_i and used directly. A negative offset yields a negative SQL OFFSET, which raises a database error and a 500. A very large or negative limit is also accepted with no cap. The endpoint is public for visible groups, so both should be clamped (for example limit between 1 and 200, offset >= 0).

findings.title: members response shape changed from a bare array to an object
findings.body: GET /groups/:id/members previously returned a JSON array, and it was unpaginated for non-automatic groups. It now returns {members, meta}. Any existing client of this public endpoint breaks, and the change is not called out in the PR description. Either version the endpoint or document the break.

findings.title: findMembers requests /members.json, changing the URL contract
findings.body: The request now adds the .json suffix and query parameters, and it always expects result.meta. Any caller relying on the old response (a plain array) or on the older URL form gets a different shape. This coupling to the new server response should be documented or covered by a test.

findings.title: coverage removed for non-existent usernames and incremental operations
findings.body: The deleted specs covered that adding a non-existent user succeeds silently, that removing a non-member succeeds, and that PATCH on automatic groups is rejected. The new add_members and remove_member specs do not cover these cases, and nothing covers the GroupsController#members pagination or meta output. Behaviour changes in these paths are now untested.

findings.title: PR description is not meaningful
findings.body: The description reads 'Test 8' and does not explain the large change: removing PATCH/PUT member updates, changing the create and update param shapes, changing the members API response, and adding paging. A reviewer cannot judge the API break from the description.
